caption: A snowman's head is knocked sideways by a thrown snowball, rolls off the body, and drops to the snow.

sa.check: A snowman stands with its head in place.
A thrown snowball hits the head.
The head is knocked sideways and rolls off the body.
The head drops to the snow.
The snowball comes in through the air.
The hit comes first, then the roll off, then the drop.

pc.expect: The head moves at the moment of impact, in the direction of the throw, and rolls off that side.
pc.fail: The head moves toward the thrower; or it moves before the snowball arrives; or it lifts straight up.

pc.expect: Once off the shoulders the head falls to the snow and stays there.
pc.fail: The head hovers above the shoulders; or rises; or bounces back onto the body.

pc.expect: The head is packed snow: it may dent, crack or break apart when it lands, and the snowball bursts or sticks.
pc.fail: The head bounces like rubber; or shatters like glass into shards; or the snowball passes through it.

pc.expect: The body stays standing and nothing else moves.
pc.fail: The body topples too with nothing hitting it; or the arms fly off; or the head rolls back up onto the body.

pc.expect: One snowman and one snowball keep their number.
pc.fail: The head vanishes or a second head appears; or the snowman turns into another object; or the snowball vanishes in flight.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The snowman's features, the scarf and the yard stay the same.
pc.fail: The face changes; or the scarf changes colour; or the yard rearranges.
